sections.content:
25,830 people

were counted on the census as "design occupations (other)" in England and Wales in March 2021.
People who do this type of work may plan, direct and undertake the creation of designs for new industrial and commercial products, stage sets, and other areas not elsewhere classified.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "design occupations (other)", 19% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "design occupations (other)" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.title: The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years
sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "design occupations (other)" included:

  • pharmacists
  • events managers and organisers
  • clothing, fashion and accessories designers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "design occupations (other)" there were a similar number of men and women (54.2% compared with 45.8%).

This means "design occupations (other)" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "culture, media and sports occupations".

Men made up 54.2% and women made up 45.8% of "design occupations (other)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "design occupations (other)" included:

  • leisure and travel service occupations (other)
  • publicans and managers of licensed premises
  • shelf fillers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "design occupations (other)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "design occupations (other)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "design occupations (other)", 9.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (78.2% compared with 21.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (68.2%) than self-employed (31.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Hackney, this is in the same region of London.
